facts.text: Tarpey Village takes its name from Patrick Tarpey, an Irish immigrant who opened a stagecoach stop on the route to Yosemite in the 1860s.
The historic Tarpey Depot, built in 1892 on the ranch, handled freight, passengers, and a post office before relocating to Old Town Clovis in the 20th century.
A 26‑mile San Joaquin Valley Railroad line, constructed in 1891 from Fresno to Friant, ran through Tarpey before being sold to Southern Pacific in 1893.
Tarpey Elementary School opened in 1958 to accommodate a growing population, a response to overcrowding in local schools during the post‑war boom.
The aviation industry spurred further residential growth in Tarpey, shifting the area’s economy and demographics toward suburban living.
Tarpey Village sits at an elevation of 351 feet, giving it a modest rise above the surrounding San Joaquin Valley plains.
